players.product: PLC-based AWG chips and AWG mux/demux for data-center optical transceivers, plus telecom DWDM AWG modules

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 half-year report (DART, consolidated): H1 revenue KRW 2,245,759,516 (H1 2025: KRW 2,085,501,711); Q2 revenue KRW 1,187,772,170 (Q2 2025: KRW 1,076,490,844); H1 operating loss KRW 1,304,104,041 (H1 2025: loss KRW 1,876,444,546); H1 net profit KRW 882,789,160 (H1 2025: net loss KRW 9,997,462,380). H1 revenue by product (KRW thousand): AWG 995,691 (44.34%), portable optical test instruments 508,852 (22.66%), OSP optical line modules 207,983 (9.26%), other products incl. optical component foundry 254,286, merchandise 278,948. By region (KRW thousand): China 798,759, Korea 614,250, US 198,019, other 634,732. Customers above 10% of revenue (undisclosed): domestic Customer A KRW 354,069 thousand, overseas Customer C KRW 620,599 thousand.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 revenue KRW 2,245,759,516 (H1 2025 KRW 2,085,501,711); H1 operating loss KRW 1,304,104,041; AWG revenue KRW 995,691 thousand (44.34%)

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and utilisation in H1 2026: data-center optical receiver modules - capacity 26,400 units with no production recorded; AWG - capacity 4,488 units, production 29, utilisation 1%; OSP optical line modules - capacity 376,200 units, production 10,494, utilisation 3%.
quarterly_data.figure: AWG utilisation 1% (29 of 4,488 units); OSP utilisation 3%; DC optical receiver module capacity 26,400 units

quarterly_data.signal: Order position at the end of H1 2026 (KRW thousand): orders received 2,489,160, delivered 2,245,759, order backlog 243,401, of which AWG 104,174, OSP 46,751, other 90,710, portable test instruments 1,765.
quarterly_data.figure: Order backlog KRW 243,401 thousand (AWG KRW 104,174 thousand)

quarterly_data.signal: Data-center AWG business (company statements): for a new overseas customer, customer evaluation of some prototypes of a changed-spec data-center DEMUX AWG and a new-spec AWG MUX was completed, chips developed in 2022 have been delivered, and the company is preparing mass production with the customer. It is in talks with new overseas customers to enter the 200G and 400G market and expects its data-center AWG to be applicable to 200G, 400G and 800G datacom transceiver modules; prices of 100G products have weakened as new makers entered. It keeps chip manufacturing in-house and outsources other module work. Since 2021 it has supplied AWG modules to global optical module suppliers in North America, Europe and China and started supplying AWG chips to AWG module makers.

Diversification outside optical components in H1 2026: the company acquired 100% of Live Connection (performance and event planning, acquired 2026.06.11) and Game Club (software development, 2026.06.22), newly established Quantum AI Solution (software) and bought into S Value Investment Partnership, bringing consolidated subsidiaries to 4.
quarterly_data.figure: 4 consolidated subsidiaries (100% of Live Connection and Game Club)

Korea Advanced Materials.why: Makes PLC-based AWG chips and mux/demux used inside data-center optical transceivers (and telecom DWDM AWG modules); AWG was 44.34% of H1 2026 revenue, so transceiver demand drives its sales.
Korea Advanced Materials.evidence: Korea Advanced Materials Q2 FY2026 (08-14-2026) half-year report: PLC chips and AWG products are mounted in transceivers inside data centers; for a new overseas customer, 2022-developed data-center AWG chips have been delivered and mass production is being prepared with the customer.
